item.title: Fort Walton Beach Doubles Down on Trash Pickup Starting Oct. 5
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Fort Walton Beach residents will soon get a break from overflowing garbage cans. Starting October 5, the city will roll out twice-weekly trash collection, up from the current once-a-week schedule, according to WKRG News 5. The expanded service is part of Fort Walton Beach's new 2-1-1 collection system, which aims to keep neighborhoods cleaner and…
item.content:encoded:
Fort Walton Beach residents will soon get a break from overflowing garbage cans. Starting October 5, the city will roll out twice-weekly trash collection, up from the current once-a-week schedule, according to WKRG News 5.

The expanded service is part of Fort Walton Beach's new 2-1-1 collection system, which aims to keep neighborhoods cleaner and reduce the buildup of refuse between pickups. The change comes as the neighboring coastal community addresses quality-of-life concerns from residents dealing with debris accumulation during Florida's warm, humid months.

While the expanded schedule may result in higher municipal costs, city leaders have prioritized the improved service to support residents and maintain neighborhood standards. Fort Walton Beach officials have not yet detailed how the enhanced collection will be funded or whether residents will see changes to their service fees.

item.content:encoded:
A Dalton, New Hampshire man faces charges after an unusual incident on August 25th involving the very emergency services responding to his home. According to reporting from Andrews McMeel, the man stole a rescue truck and used it to ram into a fire engine while firefighters were actively battling a fire at his own residence.

The bizarre sequence of events unfolded as crews worked to contain the house fire. Instead of allowing responders to do their job, authorities say the man commandeered a rescue vehicle and used it as a battering ram against one of the fire engines on scene.

The man is now in custody facing charges related to the incident. The specific charges and circumstances that led to his actions have not been fully detailed, but the case stands out as a stark example of interference with emergency services during a critical situation.

It's a methodical craft that reflects a broader philosophy about art-making rooted in the region itself.

Her work appears to be gaining attention as Pensacola's art scene continues to expand. Paux's involvement in local art nights and community events positions her as one of the area's emerging creative voices, offering both finished pieces and the story of their creation.

item.title: Chief Winstrom Explains His Flip on Flock Cameras — And What He Wants From Lawmakers Next
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police Chief Eric Winstrom joined Pensacola's Morning News Wednesday to walk through the decision to shut down the city's Flock license plate reader cameras, a day after Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Department of Transportation moved to pull the technology off state roads across Florida.…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police Chief Eric Winstrom joined Pensacola's Morning News Wednesday to walk through the decision to shut down the city's Flock license plate reader cameras, a day after Governor Ron DeSantis and the Florida Department of Transportation moved to pull the technology off state roads across Florida.


Winstrom says he'd been a supporter of the cameras throughout his time as chief, but one word from the governor's Monday remarks changed his thinking. DeSantis specifically invoked COVID while explaining his concerns about surveillance overreach, and Winstrom says that sent him back to a specific stretch of his career leading police operations in Chicago.


He described a sequence of events from late May 2020. A day after George Floyd's death in Minneapolis, a group of Chicago residents held a protest downtown against the city's COVID lockdowns. Winstrom says the mayor's office ordered police to arrest everyone involved, despite the protesters exercising their First Amendment rights. Officers ultimately talked the group into dispersing without making arrests. Three days later, when the first major protest referencing George Floyd's death arrived downtown, Winstrom says city hall gave the opposite instruction, giving the crowd space rather than intervening. That gathering spiraled into days of rioting that left roughly 70 buildings burned down.


Winstrom says that contrast is what worries him about handing a tool like Flock to leadership he doesn't personally know or trust, and it's what ultimately convinced him a legislative fix is necessary rather than leaving the decision to individual departments.


He predicts the loss of the cameras won't necessarily cause a spike in crime, but he expects Pensacola's case clearance rate to drop, since detectives use the technology on cases ranging from shoplifting to homicide.


Winstrom laid out what he'd like to see if state lawmakers take up legislation on the issue. He wants a shorter data retention window, saying most of the tool's investigative value comes within the first hour or two after a plate is captured. He also wants some form of statewide accountability standard, since he can hold his own officers responsible for how they use the system but has no way to verify what officers from outside agencies are actually looking for when they request access to Pensacola's camera network. He explained that access currently works on a reciprocal basis between agencies, meaning departments that want to use Pensacola's cameras generally have to allow Pensacola to use theirs in return.


Winstrom also addressed criticism directed at Mayor D.C. Reeves over the decision, saying the mayor had essentially no involvement in it. He says Reeves gave no pushback and left the call entirely in his hands as the department's policing expert, which Winstrom says has been his experience with Reeves on operational decisions generally.

item.title: Trump Nominates Hung Cao for Permanent Navy Secretary
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- President Trump has nominated Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao (COW) to become the permanent Secretary of the Navy, following months of Pentagon turmoil over shipbuilding priorities that led to former Secretary John Phelan's departure. Trump is urging quick Senate confirmation. Locally, shipbuilding remains a big…
item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- President Trump has nominated Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao (COW) to become the permanent Secretary of the Navy, following months of Pentagon turmoil over shipbuilding priorities that led to former Secretary John Phelan's departure. Trump is urging quick Senate confirmation. Locally, shipbuilding remains a big focus for the Navy right here in Pensacola, where Australian company Birdon is building a two-hundred-seventy-five-million-dollar facility at the Port of Pensacola to produce Navy ship and submarine modules. The project is expected to bring around two-thousand jobs to the area. Cao has recently drawn attention for meeting with families of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which just completed a record-long deployment supporting operations in Iran.

Detailed scheduling and performance lineups are expected to be announced as the October event approaches. Organizers encourage locals and visitors to mark their calendars for what's shaping up to be one of fall's marquee events on Pensacola Beach.

item.title: Pensacola's Free People's Law School Opens Legal Education to Community
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A new seminar series launching in Pensacola is making legal education accessible to everyday residents who might otherwise struggle to understand their rights and responsibilities. The Free People's Law School is bringing practical knowledge about the law directly to community members through what organizers describe as a simplified, jargon-free…
item.content:encoded:
A new seminar series launching in Pensacola is making legal education accessible to everyday residents who might otherwise struggle to understand their rights and responsibilities. The Free People's Law School is bringing practical knowledge about the law directly to community members through what organizers describe as a simplified, jargon-free approach.

According to WKRG News 5, the program focuses on real-world legal issues that affect Pensacola residents—from tenant rights and employment law to family matters and small business questions. The seminars are designed for people without legal backgrounds who want to understand the system better.

"We're trying to demystify the law," one organizer explained, emphasizing that the goal is empowerment through education rather than providing formal legal advice. The sessions tackle issues that community members face regularly but often don't know how to navigate.

The free seminars represent an effort to close a gap in legal literacy across the area. By teaching residents their rights and how the legal system works, organizers hope to help people make better-informed decisions and advocate more effectively for themselves and their families.

item.title: Baldwin County warns of Planning & Zoning scam targeting applicants

item.content:encoded:
Baldwin County officials are alerting residents to a scam that's specifically targeting people with pending applications before the Planning and Zoning Board, according to WKRG News 5.

The scheme appears designed to exploit property owners and developers navigating the local permitting process. County commissioners have urged residents to be cautious when they receive unsolicited contact regarding their zoning applications.

While details on the specific tactics used by scammers remain limited, the warning serves as a reminder for Escambia County residents to verify the legitimacy of any communication claiming to represent local government agencies. Legitimate Planning and Zoning Board correspondence typically comes directly from official county channels.

Residents with questions about the validity of communications regarding their applications are advised to contact the Baldwin County Planning and Zoning Board directly rather than responding to suspicious contacts.

item.content:encoded:
A Chickasaw family is rebuilding after a lightning strike sparked a fire that destroyed their home during severe weather last month. According to WKRG News 5, resident Shavelle Campbell said the family considers themselves fortunate to have escaped without injuries, even as they grapple with the total loss of their belongings and residence.

The fire spread rapidly through the structure, leaving the family to piece together their next steps in the aftermath. Campbell described how the destruction happened in moments when the lightning struck during the powerful storm system that moved through the area.

The family now faces the challenges of temporary housing, insurance claims, and the long process of rebuilding. Local emergency responders were able to contain the fire, though the home was already a total loss by the time crews arrived.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos couldn't pull out a tight one Tuesday night, dropping a 3-2 decision to the Columbus Clingstones in the opening game of their final regular-season road series.

The matchup turned into a pitcher's duel, with Clingstones starter Zebrowski keeping Pensacola's bats relatively quiet through most of the contest. Despite the low-scoring affair, the Blue Wahoos managed to stay competitive throughout, but ultimately came up one run short in the loss.

The defeat marks another tight game for Pensacola as the team winds down its regular season on the road. The Blue Wahoos will continue their series against Columbus as they look to bounce back in upcoming games.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's locally owned Cat Country 98.7 radio station and its signature morning program have both earned nominations for Country Music Association Awards, according to North Escambia reporting.

WYCT – Cat Country 98.7 and The Cat Pak Morning Show will compete in their respective CMA Award categories. The nominations recognize the station's programming and on-air talent in the country music format.

The CMA Awards, one of the music industry's most prominent honors, celebrate excellence across country radio and recording. Local recognition in the awards reflects the station's standing within the competitive country music broadcasting landscape.

The station has built a reputation as a community-focused outlet, and these nominations underscore its reach and influence in the Pensacola market.
